title: Balanced Binary Tree
statement:
Given a binary tree, determine if it is **height-balanced**: a binary tree in which the depth of the two subtrees of every node never differs by more than one.

Build a real `TreeNode` tree from `values`, then run a single post-order DFS that computes each subtree's height while short-circuiting to a sentinel value as soon as an imbalance is found anywhere below.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 5000]

editorial.approach: Compute height recursively (post-order). At each node, get the left and right subtree heights; if the absolute difference exceeds 1 anywhere in the tree, mark the whole tree as unbalanced (a boolean flag, or a sentinel like -1 propagated upward to short-circuit further recursion once found). Return the height as usual (1 + max of children) so the parent call can keep checking balance further up.
